description: The rabbitfish is a chimaera with a cartilage skeleton, a long tapering tail, and permanent tooth plates for crushing shellfish.

Reported maximum length 150 cm and weight 2.5 kg; the rabbitfish is the representative species.
Research-trawl sample of females: up to 190 cm and 12,600 g. Rounded upper reference values, not a matched individual.
Published maximum mass 346 kg, rounded to 760 lb.
FishBase maximum published mass 109.6 kg; rounded to 240 lb.

Luo-Ascorbe (2004), Table 6: monthly mean wet body masses 140.7–176.8 g in 6.1–8 cm test-diameter animals. Reference adult test diameter about 3 in and weight about 160 g; excludes spine length from the size measurement.

description: The magnificent anemone anchors to reef rock with a sticky foot. Its stinging tentacles catch prey and shelter several species of anemonefish.

Typical oral disc 30–50 cm; 16 in is a rounded reference within that range. A 357 g Heteractis magnifica specimen was used in the settlement-cue study; weight is a specimen reference, not a species mean. Accepted name Radianthus magnifica.

SEAMAP 2012 summer shrimp/groundfish survey Table 2: 247 individuals, aggregate mass 0.5 kg; 500/247 = 2.02 g per sampled crab. Approximate survey mean, not a mass measured for the maximum 9.5-in span.

description: Peacock mantis shrimp smash hard-shelled prey with club-like limbs. Their rapid strikes create cavitation bubbles that collapse in a second impact.

The Cousteau Society lists 10–18 cm length and up to 90 g. Rounded upper size reference.
Prince William Sound ecosystem report estimates average wet weight about 75 g (T. Dean data). Sample/population reference, not the weight of a maximum-size star.
Choi/Choe 2018 experiment: 336 animals, mean length 42.8 ± 2.3 mm and mean mass 2.23 ± 0.15 g.
Frontiers 2022 study: average shell length 28.7 cm, average live whole weight 2.57 kg. Includes shell.

description: Greater blue-ringed octopuses flash vivid blue rings when threatened. These small reef hunters use potent venom to subdue crabs and other prey.

Artwork has yellow skin and conspicuous blue rings. ADW: arm spread to 20 cm, mass range 10–100 g. Uses upper reference values.

description: Eastern oysters filter plankton from coastal water. Their rough shells grow together into reefs that shelter fish, crabs, and other small animals.

2025 breeding-population study of 3,653 oysters: mean whole weight 47.50 g. Includes shell. Shell length to be confirmed from Table 1 before apply.

description: The swimming sea cucumber feeds on seafloor sediment, then swims with a webbed veil. Its transparent body reveals the coiled gut inside.

Bailey et al. 1994 Table 1: 58 animals, mean longitudinal length 131.6 mm and mean wet mass 284.9 g.

description: Common brittle stars raise their spiny arms to catch food particles from passing water. A lost arm can regrow after a narrow escape.

Blanchet-Aurigny et al. 2012: O. fragilis with 1.5-cm discs; Figure 2 wet masses near 1 g. Rounded graph estimate. Disc diameter explicitly excludes arms.
Vampire blood (1999) experimental specimens explicitly had estimated weight 250 g each. A published estimate, not a species maximum.
Exuma Sound experiment: length range 17.6–35.8 cm and mass 181–1,097 g; rounded upper sample references.
Sizing Ocean Giants cites Fisher et al. (1988): large worms reach 650 g wet body mass. Existing 8-ft measure refers to tube length, now labeled explicitly; weight excludes tube.

description: Boreal glass squid have transparent bodies and large eyes. Light organs beneath the eyes help conceal their silhouettes in the dim ocean.

2018 fatty-acid prey study: two T. borealis, mean mantle length 38.8 cm and mean whole mass 168.45 g.

Molina-Ramírez et al. 2015 Table I: geometric mean wet colony mass 2.78 g for 18 sampled colonies. This is a small-colony reference, independent of the long tentacle-length reference; not maximum species weight.
SeaLifeBase maximum published whole mass 148 g; NOAA confirms total length to 12 in, including arms.
ADW reports maximum mass 2 kg. Rounded to 4.4 lb.

description: Singapore parrotfish graze reef surfaces with fused, beak-like teeth. Terminal-phase fish have a distinctive green throat and brightly edged scales.

Representative chosen for green throat and colorful scale edges. FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.01122×L(cm)^3.06 at 50.8 cm; about 1.86 kg, rounded 4.1 lb. This is a model estimate based on genus/body shape.
Published sample LWR a=0.0065, b=3.168 (20.5–30 cm); W=0.0065×25.4^3.168 g. Uses a 10-in reference within observed length range, rounded estimate.

description: Giant frogfish blend into sponges and reef growth, then lure prey with a modified fin spine. An expanding mouth pulls the victim in with a sudden gulp.

FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.02692×L(cm)^2.96 at 30.48 cm. Rounded model estimate based on family/body shape.
FishBase maximum total length 104 cm and maximum published mass 3.0 kg; rounded upper reference values.
FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.01995×L(cm)^3.01 at 17.78 cm (7-in female). Body-shape model estimate, not a measured adult maximum.
FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.01995×L(cm)^3.01 at 17.78 cm. Body-shape model estimate.
FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.00389×L(cm)^3.12 at 22.86 cm. Body-shape model estimate, excludes a distended stomach full of prey.
FishBase Bayesian W(g)=0.00490×L(cm)^3.03 at 43.18 cm. Family/body-shape model estimate.

description: Ballyhoo halfbeaks swim near the surface with a long lower jaw and a short upper jaw. They feed on drifting plants and small animals.

Primary study n=432: mean TL 21.26 cm, mean whole mass 46.07 g. Rounded paired sample means.

description: Hound needlefish hunt near the surface with long jaws lined with sharp teeth. They chase small fish and may leap clear of the water.

FishBase maximum total length 150 cm and maximum published weight 6.4 kg; rounded upper reference values.
